questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had visited Kobe once before and had a great time in the city. It was important to me to be in a less crowded city and with Kobe being close to both the sea and mountains it was a great place to study. It's also close to both Osaka, Nara and Kyoto.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a bit suprised that they didn't have computer support for students at campus but other than that they were extremely helpfull.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: They were very accomedating and there was email support as well as tutors helping us every step of the way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of help from my assigned tutor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would have liked an explanation of why we were filling out so many papers for the City Hall.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We just sent in an application through the university and were allocated a dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The commute takes about an hour from most of the dorms and therefore can be a bit expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in Hakuo Dormitory and loved it but unfortunately I heard that it will be torn down to build a new dorm.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was difficult but there was help whenever we needed or wanted it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to sign up for a variety of different insurances as well as the national helath insurance. Kobe University also provides a thorough list of whats needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tutors and support over email as well as a help office at the University.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get all the classes that i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a look at the classes before hand and make a list of the ones you want to try. The first week is for trying different classes and after that you sing up. If you cannot figure out how to do so, just email the support and they should help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was happy for the most part but i wish the criteria was clearer for the different classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There was a lot of classes for both BA and MA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching for the Japanese Language classes were akin to danish highschool classes. Less discussion based.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the Japanese classes i took were appropriate for about N4-N3, i would also recommend the english classes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I traveled a lot which is why i spend a lot on transportation and food, but it is possible to live very cheap in Kobe.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fruits are really expensive but orange juice is super cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate much in the non-academic opportunities at my University since i was only there for 1 semester but there were a lot.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Language cafes, sports clubs, study places, exhange student events, free trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make sure to talk to a lot of peope in the first week as thats when most other exchange students make groups to make plans. There is also tutor lead trips to different locations that are a lot of fun to participare in.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Kobe is close to a lot of fun lokations and its easy to take trips. Osaka, Nara, Kyoto are some of them but places like Himeji and Kinosaki onsen are also fun places to go. They are easy to reach by train or with highway busses service like Willer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join different social groups and classes that have both Japanese students and International.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most things are easy enough to overcome. I can't remember any in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Good cheap food. As well as beautiful preserved nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to travel.
Try as much food as you can.
Get involved in the University life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the help desk or tutors for anything, even travel recommendations.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of friends i can see in the future.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the different style of teaching.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I hope whoever reads this will want to come to Kobe University!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
